# CLI reference

See the systems in your codebase, and how a change reshapes them, without reading code. Every command, its arguments and their help, as `projections help COMMAND` prints them.
[Run projections locally](../runner/commands.md) shows how they fit together.

## Global options

These apply to every command.

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `-C, --directory <DIR>` | Run as if started in DIR, any directory of the repository. Default: `.`. |
| `--root <DIR>` | The project: the directory whose .github/projections (or .projections) holds the definitions. Default: the nearest one from the -C directory up to the repository's root. |

## `projections explore`

Find the projections that apply here and try them on recent changes.

```sh
projections explore [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `--list` | Print only the candidates. |
| `--sweep` | Try the candidates (and the projections already adopted) on recent changes and print what each shows. |
| `-p, --projection <ID>` | With --sweep, the projections to try. Default: the candidates and adopted projections. Repeatable. |
| `--last <N>` | The recent changes to sweep: merges into the current branch when it takes changes by merging, else first-parent commits (1-100). Default: `20`. |
| `--concurrency <N>` | Extractor processes to run at once. Default: `2`. |
| `--json` | With --list or --sweep, print JSON. |
| `--trust` | With --sweep, let candidates and projections that run repository code run. |

## `projections adopt`

Keep explored projections: write their definitions and bookmark their best changes.

```sh
projections adopt [OPTIONS] <ID>...
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<ID>...` | The candidates to adopt (see projections explore --list). Required. |
| `--bookmarks <N>` | Bookmark each projection's N most-changed recent changes (0 sweeps nothing). Default: `3`. |
| `--last <N>` | The recent changes to look for them in (1-100). Default: `20`. |
| `--dry-run` | Print what would be written, writing nothing. |
| `--trust` | Let candidates that run repository code extract, to find their bookmarks. |
| `--json` | Print the result as JSON. |

## `projections init`

Scaffold a projection, or add a part to one, and the agent skill.

```sh
projections init [OPTIONS] [ID]
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<ID>` | Projection ID: letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-' (for example service-map). |
| `--title <TITLE>` | Title viewers show. Default: from the ID. |
| `--language <LANGUAGE>` | Scaffold a starter extractor in this language. Default: the repository's toolchain. One of: `node` — A Node.js ES module (extract.mjs); `python` — A Python 3 script (extract.py); `go` — A Go program (extract.go, run with go run). |
| `--extractor <ID>` | Use this built-in extractor (projections extractor list shows them). |
| `--input <NAME=VALUE>` | With --extractor, set one of its inputs: NAME=VALUE, VALUE being JSON or else a string (for example workflowPath=.github/workflows/release.yml). Repeatable. |
| `--command <ARGV_JSON>` | Use this existing program as the extractor: a JSON argv array, for example '["ruby","tools/flags.rb"]'. |
| `--renderer <NAME\|custom>` | A built-in renderer name (for example graph, dag, database; projections help authoring lists them), or `custom` to scaffold one. |
| `--comparator <custom>` | Scaffold a custom comparator: a starter comparator file (<ID>.comparator.yaml) and its tests. One of `custom`. |
| `--definition-directory <DEFINITION_DIRECTORY>` | Where the definition goes. One of `.github/projections`, `.projections`. Default: `.github/projections`. |
| `--skills-dir <DIR>` | The skills directory the agent skill goes in, relative to the repository root. Default: the one holding it, else whichever of .agents/skills, .claude/skills and .github/skills holds the repository's own skills, else .agents/skills. |
| `--claude <HOW>` | Also put the skill where Claude Code reads it, .claude/skills: a symlink, or a copy on Windows (or with copy). One of: `auto` — A relative symlink to the skill, or a copy on Windows; `link` — A relative symlink to the skill; `copy` — A copy, which later runs of init keep in sync (for checkouts without symlinks). |
| `--no-skill` | Don't write, update or move the agent skill; projections help authoring prints its guide. |

## `projections check`

Verify projections end to end: extraction, comparison and renderer checks.

```sh
projections check [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `-p, --projection <ID>` | The projections to check. Default: every one the working tree defines. Repeatable. |
| `--png <FILE>` | Also write a PNG of the (one) projection's working tree, drawn by its renderer. |
| `--from <FILE>` | Check this extractor output (what the extractor writes to stdout) for the one projection instead of extracting the working tree; nothing runs, so hand-made extractions can be drawn and checked. |
| `--no-render` | Skip the renderer checks, which need Chrome, Chromium or Edge. |
| `--browser <PATH>` | Chrome, Chromium or Edge executable. Default: PROJECTIONS_BROWSER, else found on PATH or in its usual install location. |
| `--timeout <SECONDS>` | Seconds the renderer checks may take on each scenario. Default: `120`. |
| `--update` | Write or rewrite the snapshots of comparator tests (never their expectations). |
| `--coverage` | Also report comparator tests' rule coverage: which of the comparator file's functions, expressions and branches the cases run, and where the rest are. |
| `--parity <REVISION>` | Also extract this commit here and compare it with CI's artifact for it (with --ci or --artifact), to find environment drift. |
| `--strict-determinism` | Fail, rather than warn, when a rerun of the working tree gives a different extraction (CI uses it for built-in extractors). |
| `--json` | Print the projections.check document. |
| `--trust` | Run repository code: the projection's extractor, on every selected revision, and its custom renderer. Review it first. |
| `--container-image <IMAGE>` | Run extractors in this locally prepared container image@sha256; never pulled. |
| `--container-engine <CONTAINER_ENGINE>` | One of `docker`, `podman`. |
| `--no-cache` | Don't read or write the persistent extraction cache. |
| `--ci` | Reuse extractions of commits from this repository's own CI runs (their projections artifact), downloaded with gh. |
| `--artifact <DIR>` | Reuse extractions from a downloaded CI artifact directory (holding projections.artifact.json); repeatable. Repeatable. |
| `--in-place` | Extract a commit that is this checkout's HEAD in place even when untracked files (such as CI's build output) are present; tracked files must be unmodified. |
| `--workspace <STRATEGY>` | Where a toolchain extractor examines a commit that isn't checked out. Default: the user configuration, the environment file's, else automatic. One of: `fresh` — A temporary full copy per run; `worktree` — A persistent linked Git worktree Projections owns, reused and kept prepared; `clone` — A worktree seeded with a copy-on-write clone of the checkout; `sparse` — A worktree holding only the definition's scope; `none` — No copies: only the cache, CI artifacts and in-place extraction. |
| `--regenerate` | Generate generated values (such as model-written summaries) again instead of reusing the generation store's text for an equal basis. |

## `projections show`

Show one revision (the working tree by default) through a projection.

```sh
projections show [OPTIONS] [REVISION]
       projections show --all [OPTIONS] [REVISION]
       projections show --from <FILE> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<REVISION>` | Revision to show: a commit, branch, tag or working-tree. Default: working-tree. |
| `-p, --projection <ID>` | The projection. Default: the only one defined. |
| `--all` | Show every projection the revision defines, keeping each one's failure. |
| `--definition-revision <REVISION>` | Apply the definition and component code from this revision, so extractions of several revisions compare. |
| `--from <FILE>` | Present a saved extraction or comparison document instead of running extractors; with -p, an extractor's raw output, which the working tree's definition of that projection normalizes, digests and validates. |
| `--json` | Print the JSON document instead of text. |
| `--output <FILE>` | Write the JSON document to a new FILE instead of printing it. |
| `--png <FILE>` | Also draw it with its real renderer in a headless browser, to a new PNG FILE. |
| `--frames <DIR>` | Comparisons: also draw the animated playback as the viewer loops it back and forth at 1× speed, from the start of its hold at the before end, as PNG frames in the new directory DIR with frames.json, which lists each frame's file, progress, direction and duration; a hold is one frame. |
| `--fps <FPS>` | Frames a second that --frames samples playback at. Default: `12`. |
| `--theme <THEME>` | One of `light`, `dark`. Default: `light`. |
| `--frame <FRAME>` | How the image frames the renderer's content. One of: `card` — One rounded card with a hairline border holding the renderer's content, its legend and the summary bar, transparent outside its corners; the image is as tall as the card, which hugs the content up to --height; `none` — The renderer's content alone, edge to edge, without the legend or the summary bar. Default: `card`. |
| `--matte <COLOR>` | Fill outside the card's rounded corners with this #rgb or #rrggbb COLOR instead of transparency, for formats without alpha such as GIF. |
| `--width <WIDTH>` | Viewport width in CSS pixels. Default: `1280`. |
| `--height <HEIGHT>` | Viewport height in CSS pixels; with --frame card, the most the image is: --png crops it to the card, which hugs the renderer's content. Default: `800`. |
| `--scale <SCALE>` | Device pixels per CSS pixel; 2 for high-density displays. Default: `1`. |
| `--progress <0..1>` | Comparisons: the transition's progress, 0 (before) to 1 (after, the default). |
| `--mode <MODE>` | Comparisons: how to present them. Default: the renderer's default, its diff when it has one; animated with --progress. One of: `animated` — One frame at a transition progress (--progress); `side-by-side` — The before and after revisions in two panes; `diff` — One frame with the renderer's own static comparison. |
| `--focus <WHAT>` | Open the image on a comparison's changes or on everything. Default: the renderer's choice; a diff opens on its changes when they don't all fit. One of: `changes` — A comparison's changed items and the relationships between them; `all` — Everything. |
| `--entity <ID>` | Open the image on one item, by its ID, centred with what it connects to. |
| `--fit` | Fit what the image opens on whole, even when its text is drawn smaller than the renderer would open at. |
| `--side <SIDE>` | Comparisons: draw one side alone, with the renderer of the definition that explained the comparison. One of `before`, `after`. |
| `--browser <PATH>` | Chrome, Chromium or Edge executable. Default: PROJECTIONS_BROWSER, else found on PATH or in its usual install location. |
| `--timeout <SECONDS>` | Seconds the renderer may take to finish painting. Default: 60, and more for large extractions. |
| `--trust` | Run repository code: the projection's extractor, on every selected revision, and its custom renderer. Review it first. |
| `--container-image <IMAGE>` | Run extractors in this locally prepared container image@sha256; never pulled. |
| `--container-engine <CONTAINER_ENGINE>` | One of `docker`, `podman`. |
| `--no-cache` | Don't read or write the persistent extraction cache. |
| `--ci` | Reuse extractions of commits from this repository's own CI runs (their projections artifact), downloaded with gh. |
| `--artifact <DIR>` | Reuse extractions from a downloaded CI artifact directory (holding projections.artifact.json); repeatable. Repeatable. |
| `--in-place` | Extract a commit that is this checkout's HEAD in place even when untracked files (such as CI's build output) are present; tracked files must be unmodified. |
| `--workspace <STRATEGY>` | Where a toolchain extractor examines a commit that isn't checked out. Default: the user configuration, the environment file's, else automatic. One of: `fresh` — A temporary full copy per run; `worktree` — A persistent linked Git worktree Projections owns, reused and kept prepared; `clone` — A worktree seeded with a copy-on-write clone of the checkout; `sparse` — A worktree holding only the definition's scope; `none` — No copies: only the cache, CI artifacts and in-place extraction. |
| `--regenerate` | Generate generated values (such as model-written summaries) again instead of reusing the generation store's text for an equal basis. |

## `projections serve`

Serve the VS Code extension over standard input and output (--stdio).

```sh
projections serve [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `--stdio` | Speak JSON-RPC 2.0 over standard input and output, one message per line (required: the only transport). |
| `--trust` | Let it run repository code (custom extractors and renderers) and write repository files. |
| `--document <FILE>` | Present a saved extraction, comparison or pull request review instead of the repository, running nothing. |
| `--fixtures <PATH>` | Serve projections.scenarios documents (or directories holding scenarios.json) for developing a renderer or comparator, instead of a repository; runs no extractors. Repeatable. |
| `--renderer <DIR>` | With --fixtures, renderer bundle directories (index.html and renderer.json), or packages whose package.json names one in projections.renderer. Repeatable. |
| `--no-cache` | Don't read or write the persistent extraction cache. |
| `--ci` | Reuse extractions of commits from this repository's own CI runs (their projections artifact), downloaded with gh. |
| `--artifact <DIR>` | Reuse extractions from a downloaded CI artifact directory (holding projections.artifact.json); repeatable. Repeatable. |
| `--in-place` | Extract a commit that is this checkout's HEAD in place even when untracked files (such as CI's build output) are present; tracked files must be unmodified. |
| `--workspace <STRATEGY>` | Where a toolchain extractor examines a commit that isn't checked out. Default: the user configuration, the environment file's, else automatic. One of: `fresh` — A temporary full copy per run; `worktree` — A persistent linked Git worktree Projections owns, reused and kept prepared; `clone` — A worktree seeded with a copy-on-write clone of the checkout; `sparse` — A worktree holding only the definition's scope; `none` — No copies: only the cache, CI artifacts and in-place extraction. |
| `--regenerate` | Generate generated values (such as model-written summaries) again instead of reusing the generation store's text for an equal basis. |

## `projections view`

Serve a projection viewer page on loopback that a coding agent drives and a person watches.

```sh
projections view [OPTIONS]
       projections view <COMMAND>
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `-p, --projection <ID>` | The projection. Default: the one shown, else the only one the repository defines. |
| `--choice <CHOICE>` | What to compare: branch, uncommitted, last-commit, now, release or bookmark:<id>. Default: the suggested pair. |
| `--before <REVISION>` | The Before revision: a branch, tag or commit, or working-tree. |
| `--after <REVISION>` | The After revision. Default: working-tree. |
| `--mode <MODE>` | The comparison mode. One of `side-by-side`, `animated`, `swipe`, `diff`. |
| `--entity <ID>` | An entity, relationship or change to select, by ID. |
| `--scenario <ID>` | A scenario from the projection's renderer scenarios, shown instead of revisions. |
| `--viewer <NAME>` | Show it in a named viewer, its own page and URL beside the others, to show several projections side by side. Default: the default viewer. |
| `--theme <SEED>` | Color the page as the app that shows it, for a harness whose surfaces the default theme doesn't match: a theme seed, inline JSON or a JSON file, `{"light": {"background": …, "border": …}, "dark": {…}}`. It goes in the printed link (`?theme=`), so only a page opened from that link takes it. Default: the page's own theme. |
| `--port <PORT>` | The port to listen on; 0 for any free one. Default: the port this project's viewer last listened on, else any free one. |
| `--open` | Also open the page in the default browser. |
| `--trust` | Let it run repository code (custom extractors and renderers). Review the projections' code first. A viewer already running without trust is replaced, at the same URL. |
| `--definition-revision <REVISION>` | The revision whose definition and projection code extract both sides, as compare --definition-revision. Default: working-tree. |
| `--no-cache` | Don't read or write the persistent extraction cache. |
| `--ci` | Reuse extractions of commits from this repository's own CI runs (their projections artifact), downloaded with gh. |
| `--artifact <DIR>` | Reuse extractions from a downloaded CI artifact directory (holding projections.artifact.json); repeatable. Repeatable. |
| `--in-place` | Extract a commit that is this checkout's HEAD in place even when untracked files (such as CI's build output) are present; tracked files must be unmodified. |
| `--workspace <STRATEGY>` | Where a toolchain extractor examines a commit that isn't checked out. Default: the user configuration, the environment file's, else automatic. One of: `fresh` — A temporary full copy per run; `worktree` — A persistent linked Git worktree Projections owns, reused and kept prepared; `clone` — A worktree seeded with a copy-on-write clone of the checkout; `sparse` — A worktree holding only the definition's scope; `none` — No copies: only the cache, CI artifacts and in-place extraction. |
| `--regenerate` | Generate generated values (such as model-written summaries) again instead of reusing the generation store's text for an equal basis. |

Its commands: [`projections view show`](#projections-view-show), [`projections view current`](#projections-view-current), [`projections view screenshot`](#projections-view-screenshot), [`projections view refresh`](#projections-view-refresh), [`projections view stop`](#projections-view-stop).

## `projections view show`

Show a projection in the viewer, starting one in the background when none runs (the open_projection tool).

```sh
projections view show [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `-p, --projection <ID>` | The projection. Default: the one shown, else the only one the repository defines. |
| `--choice <CHOICE>` | What to compare: branch, uncommitted, last-commit, now, release or bookmark:<id>. Default: the suggested pair. |
| `--before <REVISION>` | The Before revision: a branch, tag or commit, or working-tree. |
| `--after <REVISION>` | The After revision. Default: working-tree. |
| `--mode <MODE>` | The comparison mode. One of `side-by-side`, `animated`, `swipe`, `diff`. |
| `--entity <ID>` | An entity, relationship or change to select, by ID. |
| `--scenario <ID>` | A scenario from the projection's renderer scenarios, shown instead of revisions. |
| `--viewer <NAME>` | Show it in a named viewer, its own page and URL beside the others, to show several projections side by side. Default: the default viewer. |
| `--theme <SEED>` | Color the page as the app that shows it, for a harness whose surfaces the default theme doesn't match: a theme seed, inline JSON or a JSON file, `{"light": {"background": …, "border": …}, "dark": {…}}`. It goes in the printed link (`?theme=`), so only a page opened from that link takes it. Default: the page's own theme. |
| `--open` | Also open the page in the default browser. |
| `--trust` | Let the viewer run repository code: one is started with trust, or replaces one running without it. |
| `--port <PORT>` | The port a viewer this starts listens on; 0 for any free one. Refused when a viewer already runs on another. Default: the port this project's viewer last listened on, else any free one. |
| `--json` | Print the result as JSON. |

## `projections view screenshot`

Render what the viewer shows to a new PNG file with its real renderer (the screenshot tool).

```sh
projections view screenshot [OPTIONS] --out <FILE>
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `--out <FILE>` | The new PNG file. Required. |
| `-p, --projection <ID>` | Another projection. Default: the one the viewer shows. |
| `--before <REVISION>` | The Before revision. Default: the viewer's. |
| `--after <REVISION>` | The After revision. Default: the viewer's. |
| `--mode <MODE>` | How to present a comparison. Default: the viewer's. One of: `animated` — One frame at a transition progress (--progress); `side-by-side` — The before and after revisions in two panes; `diff` — One frame with the renderer's own static comparison. |
| `--progress <0..1>` | Animated mode: the transition's progress, 0 to 1. Default: the viewer's playback position. |
| `--theme <THEME>` | . Default: the page's. One of `light`, `dark`. |
| `--width <WIDTH>` | Viewport width in CSS pixels. Default: the page's, else 1280. |
| `--height <HEIGHT>` | Viewport height in CSS pixels, the most the image is: it is as tall as its card, which hugs the content. Default: the page's, else 800. |
| `--focus <WHAT>` | Open the image on a comparison's changes or on everything. Default: the renderer's choice. One of: `changes` — A comparison's changed items and the relationships between them; `all` — Everything. |
| `--entity <ID>` | Open the image on one item, by its ID, centred with what it connects to. |
| `--fit` | Fit what the image opens on whole, even when its text is drawn smaller than the renderer would open at. |
| `--viewer <NAME>` | Render what a named viewer shows. Default: the default viewer. |
| `--page` | Capture the viewer's page itself, its header, toolbar and summary bar around the projection, as a page opened now shows it: the viewer's projection, pair, mode and selection, not the person's playback position or zoom. |
| `--json` | Print the result as JSON. |

## `projections view refresh`

Extract what the viewer shows again (the refresh tool).

```sh
projections view refresh [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `--viewer <NAME>` | A named viewer. Default: the default viewer. |
| `--json` | Print the result as JSON. |

## `projections view stop`

Stop the viewer running for this repository; its open pages say so, and reconnect if one starts at its URL.

```sh
projections view stop [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `--rotate` | Also forget its link: the next viewer has a new token (and port), and every earlier link stops working. |

## `projections canvas`

Add the viewer to the GitHub Copilot app as a canvas, for this repository.

```sh
projections canvas [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

Its commands: [`projections canvas install`](#projections-canvas-install).

## `projections canvas install`

Writes the Projections canvas extension to .github/extensions/projections/extension.mjs, where the GitHub Copilot app (and Copilot CLI) load it for this repository. Its canvas shows the viewer (projections view) in the app's side panel, and its actions are the open_projection, current_view, screenshot and refresh tools. It runs the projections CLI on PATH, or PROJECTIONS_CLI. Commit it to share it with the repository's contributors. An existing file is replaced only with --force.

```sh
projections canvas install [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `--force` | Replace an existing extension file. |

## `projections list`

List the projections a revision defines, running nothing.

```sh
projections list [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `--revision <REVISION>` | The revision whose definitions to list. Default: `working-tree`. |
| `--json` | Print the JSON document instead of text. |

## `projections compare`

Compare two revisions, or one revision with the working tree.

```sh
projections compare [OPTIONS] <BASE>[..<HEAD>]
       projections compare --all [OPTIONS] <BASE>[..<HEAD>]
       projections compare --before-extraction <FILE> --after-extraction <FILE> [-p <ID>] [--comparator <FILE>]
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<RANGE>` | <BASE>[..<HEAD>] or <BASE>...<HEAD>. |
| `-p, --projection <ID>` | The projection. Default: the only one defined. |
| `--all` | Compare every projection either revision defines, keeping each one's failure. |
| `--definition <DEFINITION>` | Which revision's projection definition and component code to apply to both revisions. One of: `base` — The first (base) revision's definition; `head` — The second (head) revision's definition. Default: `base`. |
| `--definition-revision <REVISION>` | Apply this revision's definition and component code to both instead, for example working-tree to try uncommitted projection code on real history. |
| `--before-extraction <FILE>` | Compare two saved extractions instead of running extractors. With -p ID, either may also be extractor output (or a saved extraction edited by hand), made a document with the working tree's definition of ID. |
| `--after-extraction <FILE>` | The saved extraction to compare with --before-extraction. |
| `--comparator <FILE>` | The custom comparator file the saved extractions' definition names [default with -p: the working tree's]. |
| `--json` | Print the JSON document instead of text. |
| `--output <FILE>` | Write the JSON document to a new FILE instead of printing it. |
| `--png <FILE>` | Also draw it with its real renderer in a headless browser, to a new PNG FILE. |
| `--frames <DIR>` | Comparisons: also draw the animated playback as the viewer loops it back and forth at 1× speed, from the start of its hold at the before end, as PNG frames in the new directory DIR with frames.json, which lists each frame's file, progress, direction and duration; a hold is one frame. |
| `--fps <FPS>` | Frames a second that --frames samples playback at. Default: `12`. |
| `--theme <THEME>` | One of `light`, `dark`. Default: `light`. |
| `--frame <FRAME>` | How the image frames the renderer's content. One of: `card` — One rounded card with a hairline border holding the renderer's content, its legend and the summary bar, transparent outside its corners; the image is as tall as the card, which hugs the content up to --height; `none` — The renderer's content alone, edge to edge, without the legend or the summary bar. Default: `card`. |
| `--matte <COLOR>` | Fill outside the card's rounded corners with this #rgb or #rrggbb COLOR instead of transparency, for formats without alpha such as GIF. |
| `--width <WIDTH>` | Viewport width in CSS pixels. Default: `1280`. |
| `--height <HEIGHT>` | Viewport height in CSS pixels; with --frame card, the most the image is: --png crops it to the card, which hugs the renderer's content. Default: `800`. |
| `--scale <SCALE>` | Device pixels per CSS pixel; 2 for high-density displays. Default: `1`. |
| `--progress <0..1>` | Comparisons: the transition's progress, 0 (before) to 1 (after, the default). |
| `--mode <MODE>` | Comparisons: how to present them. Default: the renderer's default, its diff when it has one; animated with --progress. One of: `animated` — One frame at a transition progress (--progress); `side-by-side` — The before and after revisions in two panes; `diff` — One frame with the renderer's own static comparison. |
| `--focus <WHAT>` | Open the image on a comparison's changes or on everything. Default: the renderer's choice; a diff opens on its changes when they don't all fit. One of: `changes` — A comparison's changed items and the relationships between them; `all` — Everything. |
| `--entity <ID>` | Open the image on one item, by its ID, centred with what it connects to. |
| `--fit` | Fit what the image opens on whole, even when its text is drawn smaller than the renderer would open at. |
| `--side <SIDE>` | Comparisons: draw one side alone, with the renderer of the definition that explained the comparison. One of `before`, `after`. |
| `--browser <PATH>` | Chrome, Chromium or Edge executable. Default: PROJECTIONS_BROWSER, else found on PATH or in its usual install location. |
| `--timeout <SECONDS>` | Seconds the renderer may take to finish painting. Default: 60, and more for large extractions. |
| `--trust` | Run repository code: the projection's extractor, on every selected revision, and its custom renderer. Review it first. |
| `--container-image <IMAGE>` | Run extractors in this locally prepared container image@sha256; never pulled. |
| `--container-engine <CONTAINER_ENGINE>` | One of `docker`, `podman`. |
| `--no-cache` | Don't read or write the persistent extraction cache. |
| `--ci` | Reuse extractions of commits from this repository's own CI runs (their projections artifact), downloaded with gh. |
| `--artifact <DIR>` | Reuse extractions from a downloaded CI artifact directory (holding projections.artifact.json); repeatable. Repeatable. |
| `--in-place` | Extract a commit that is this checkout's HEAD in place even when untracked files (such as CI's build output) are present; tracked files must be unmodified. |
| `--workspace <STRATEGY>` | Where a toolchain extractor examines a commit that isn't checked out. Default: the user configuration, the environment file's, else automatic. One of: `fresh` — A temporary full copy per run; `worktree` — A persistent linked Git worktree Projections owns, reused and kept prepared; `clone` — A worktree seeded with a copy-on-write clone of the checkout; `sparse` — A worktree holding only the definition's scope; `none` — No copies: only the cache, CI artifacts and in-place extraction. |
| `--regenerate` | Generate generated values (such as model-written summaries) again instead of reusing the generation store's text for an equal basis. |

| `--ci` | Reuse extractions of commits from this repository's own CI runs (their projections artifact), downloaded with gh. |

| `--in-place` | Extract a commit that is this checkout's HEAD in place even when untracked files (such as CI's build output) are present; tracked files must be unmodified. |
| `--workspace <STRATEGY>` | Where a toolchain extractor examines a commit that isn't checked out. Default: the user configuration, the environment file's, else automatic. One of: `fresh` — A temporary full copy per run; `worktree` — A persistent linked Git worktree Projections owns, reused and kept prepared; `clone` — A worktree seeded with a copy-on-write clone of the checkout; `sparse` — A worktree holding only the definition's scope; `none` — No copies: only the cache, CI artifacts and in-place extraction. |
| `--regenerate` | Generate generated values (such as model-written summaries) again instead of reusing the generation store's text for an equal basis. |

## `projections pr`

Review a GitHub pull request without running its code.

```sh
projections pr [OPTIONS] <NUMBER|URL>
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<NUMBER\|URL>` | The pull request: a number or URL. Required. |
| `-R, --repo <[HOST/]OWNER/REPO>` | The repository: [HOST/]OWNER/REPO. Default: from the URL, or this checkout's origin remote. |
| `--id <ID>` | Compare only these projections. Repeatable. |
| `--cache <DIR>` | The parent directory for the isolated acquisition working directory. |
| `--json` | Print the JSON document instead of text. |
| `--output <FILE>` | Write the JSON document to a new FILE instead of printing it. |
